test_plan.title: Add caching (orbit-geo) to Country reference/lookup reads
test_plan.steps:
- Load a page with a Country dropdown/pick-list (e.g. user profile, address form) and verify the list populates correctly with active countries in alphabetical order.
- Edit a Country record in the admin interface (e.g. change name, toggle IsActive status) and save; then reload a page with the Country dropdown and confirm the change is reflected immediately.
- Monitor Cosmos DB RU consumption for `Country` reads during normal page load activity and verify it is significantly lower than the baseline ~28k RU reported before caching was implemented.
- Deactivate a Country record via admin interface and verify it no longer appears in Country dropdowns on subsequently loaded pages.
- Load the same page with a Country dropdown multiple times in quick succession and confirm response times are consistent/fast (indicating cache hits).

test_plan.title: Add caching (orbit-geo) to State reference/lookup reads
test_plan.steps:
- Load a page with a State dropdown/pick-list (e.g., a form that displays active states) and verify states load and display correctly.
- Edit a State record in the admin panel (change name, toggle IsActive status) and save; then refresh the dropdown page and confirm the updated state appears immediately without stale data.
- Monitor RU consumption in CosmosDB for the `orbit-geo` database during repeated page loads with State dropdowns; verify RU usage is significantly lower than the baseline ~28k RU (caching should reduce read volume).
- Clear the application cache (restart the app or invalidate manually if exposed), then load a State dropdown and verify it re-populates from the database and displays correctly.
- On a multi-instance deployment (if applicable), edit a State on one instance and verify all instances reflect the change within a reasonable timeframe (if using Option B/Redis) or after cache expiration (if using Option A/in-process).

test_plan.title: Notification report (sent notification) view returns 500 when a response has a null Employee
test_plan.steps:
- Navigate to a notification event report (via /setting/customer/{id}/notification/view/{subId} or /notification/event/view/{id}) that contains at least one response with a null Employee field
- Verify the page loads successfully with HTTP 200 and the response table renders without throwing a 500 error
- Confirm that rows with valid Employee display the person's name sorted by last name then first name
- Confirm that rows with null Employee display a placeholder text (e.g. "Unknown employee") instead of a name and do not have a clickable profile link
- Verify the same behavior works for both "Response Required: Yes" and "Response Required: No" notification events

test_plan.title: Fix Notification SMS and Mobile Check-In Verification
test_plan.steps:
- Enter an incorrect verification code in the verification box and verify that it is rejected
- Enter the correct verification code that was sent to the device and verify that it is accepted
- Trigger the resend verification code button and confirm the code is sent to the Notification SMS number (not the Mobile Check-In number)
- Complete verification and confirm the success message is sent to the Notification SMS number (not the Mobile Check-In number)

sprint_report.goals: This sprint focused on improving system reliability and user experience in employee verification workflows while enhancing overall application performance through strategic caching enhancements across reference data lookups.
sprint_report.summary: The team resolved critical issues in the mobile and SMS verification pipeline, including proper handling of notification responses and improved input parsing for check-in data. Users now receive clear feedback on verification status directly within their profile pages. To strengthen the foundation for these improvements and future development, comprehensive unit test coverage was added across core entity classes. Additionally, a systematic caching strategy was implemented across thirty-two reference and lookup data types using dedicated cache layers, significantly reducing database load and improving response times for employee, geographic, rank, and administrative reference data that are accessed frequently throughout the application.
